LESSON: PATTERNS CLASSIFICATION

Grade: PP1
Subject: MATHEMATICS ACTIVITIES
Strand: Strand 1
Topic 1.4: Patterns CLASSIFICATION

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello learner! Today we will learn about Patterns CLASSIFICATION. Read carefully, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

Big question: which pattern make a pattern?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify similarities in patterns in the environment
2. identify different patterns in the environment
3. identify the repeated shapes which form a pattern e) arrange similar objects to make a pattern f) arrange 2 different objects in an alternating manner to make patterns shapes on their clothes, foot prints, g) appreciate the different types of buildings, flower gardens etc objects in the environment h) enjoy making different patterns same shape with two different colours with objects found in the environment. with objects of same type with two different colours. using ICT devices to make patterns devices.

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

1. identify similarities in patterns in the environment
   In this part of the lesson, you learn to identify similarities in patterns in the environment. Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

2. identify different patterns in the environment
   In this part of the lesson, you learn to identify different patterns in the environment. Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

3. identify the repeated shapes which form a pattern e) arrange similar objects to make a pattern f) arrange 2 different objects in an alternating manner to make patterns shapes on their clothes, foot prints, g) appreciate the different types of buildings, flower gardens etc objects in the environment h) enjoy making different patterns same shape with two different colours with objects found in the environment. with objects of same type with two different colours. using ICT devices to make patterns devices.

Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: At the market in your county, count 10 mangoes. Put them in 2 groups of 5. That is sorting and grouping.

Example 2: In class, count the desks in your row. Write the number in figures and in words.

Example 3: If you have 7 shillings and your parent gives you 5 more, you have 12 shillings. That is addition.

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Read the examples above again. Underline two new words or ideas about Patterns CLASSIFICATION.
2. Explain Patterns CLASSIFICATION to a parent or classmate using your own words and one Kenyan example.
3. Draw or write three things that show you understand Patterns CLASSIFICATION.
4. Show that you can: identify similarities in patterns in the environment
5. Complete the Work to do section, then attempt the Revision Quiz. Check Answers only after you finish.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Patterns CLASSIFICATION. Use examples from your school, home, or market.
2. Answer this question in your exercise book: which pattern make a pattern?
3. Make a short oral presentation (about one minute) to your parent or teacher.
4. List three ways you will practise this topic this week.

SECTION 8: REMEMBER

1. identify similarities in patterns in the environment
2. identify different patterns in the environment
3. identify the repeated shapes which form a pattern e) arrange similar objects to make a pattern f) arrange 2 different objects in an alternating manner to make patterns shapes on their clothes, foot prints, g) appreciate the different types of buildings, flower gardens etc objects in the environment h) enjoy making different patterns same shape with two different colours with objects found in the environment. with objects of same type with two different colours. using ICT devices to make patterns devices.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.
